text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
WHEAT SALE - Australia has sold 150,000 tonnes of wheat to Iraq for March shipment, the Australian Wheat Board said. The purchase price was not disclosed.

- Tunisia purchased 125,000 tonnes of soft wheat for March-April shipment at $158.77 and $156.76 per tonne C&F, traders said. The purchased was divided into five 25,000 tonne positions. The first shipment is slated for March 1-10, the second for March 10-20, the third for March 20-30, and two for April 1-10.

WHEAT, BARLEY SALE - The Japanese Food Agency bought 120,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, 40,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat and 20,000 tonnes of Australian wheat for March shipment at its weekly tender. The agency also bought 20,000 tonnes of U.S. barley and 36,000 tonnes of Australian barley.

WHEAT SALE - Two South Korean firms bought a total of 22,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat from Misubishi of Japan. One firm bought 9,000 tonnes was purchased basis May U.S. wheat futures for shipment for March 10 to April 10. The other 13,000 tonnes was purchased at flat prices, traders said.

CORN SALES - The Korean Feed Association bought 52,500 tonnes of U.S. and Chinese corn from Cargill and 105,000 tonnes of Argentine, U.S. and Chinese corn from Toepfer, traders said. Shipment dates ranged from February 9 through April 29, and prices ranged from $129.00 to $140.90 per tonne.

- Several South Korean feed millers bought 52,500 tonnes of U.S. No. 3 yellow corn from Peavey, traders said. Traders said 40,000 tonnes was priced at $139.90 per tonne, and the rest went for 88 cents per bushel over May CBOT futures. Shipment was set for March 20-April 10 from the U.S. PNW.

RICE SALE - Malaysia bought 20,000 tonnes of sticky rice and 100 percent grade B rice from Thailand for February-March shipment, traders said. The sticky rice was sold at $450 per tonne FOB Bangkok and the 100 percent grade was $360 per tonne.

SOYOIL SALE - China bought 13,500 tonnes of Argentine soyoil, U.S. exporters said. The purchase, in three shipments of 4,500 tonnes each for May, June and July, was priced at $512.00 a tonne, exporters said.
WHEAT TENDERS - India will tender for 50,000 tonnes of wheat by the end of March. The tender closes January 29.
- Jordan will tender on February 5 for 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat or equivalent origin for shipment by March 31, traders said. U.S. wheat be under the GSM 102 program said.

- Moroccan importers passed on offers for 12,000 tonnes of optional-origin milling wheat, traders said. Another tender for 15,000 tonnes will be held Thursday, with shipment set for February 25 through March 5.
- Results were awaited on Bangladesh's tender for 100,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 wheat or Australian or Canadian winter red/spring wheat for shipment by February 21, traders said.
- Lebanon's economy ministry plans to buy 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat later this month, the government said.

BARLEY/WHEAT TENDER - The Cyprus Grain Commission has invited tenders for one shipment of 12,000 tonnes of European milling wheat and one of 25,000 tonnes of barley. Shipment was March 13 to 28 for the wheat and February for the barley.
CORN TENDER - News was awaited on South Africa's Maize Board's tender for 15,000 tonnes of yellow maize for either export or domestic use. The offer was seen closing January 16.
- South Korea's NLCF said Thursday it passed on tenders for 52,500 of No. 3 yellow corn due to high offers, traders said.
- Algeria seeks 30,000 tonnes of U.S. or Argentine maize in two equal shipments of 15,000 tonnes, grain traders said on Thursday. Shipment is for February 10-28.
RICE TENDER - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organization for Chemicals and Foodstuffs is seeking to buy 12,000 tonnes of white rice for March shipment. Results would be February 13.

SOYBEAN TENDERS - South Korea's state-run Agricultural and Fishery Marketing Corp invited tenders for 40,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 1 soybeans on January 29. Shipment of one 20,000 purchase will be for January 30 to February 18 from the U.S. Gulf or from February 14 to March 5 from the U.S. Pacific Northwest. Shipment of the other 20,000 tonnes will be from the U.S. Gulf between February 24 to March 15 or from PNW March 11 to 30.
- Taiwan's BSPA will tender Friday for 54,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans for shipment from the U.S. Gulf between February 26 and March 12, or from the Pacific Northwest from March 13 to 27.

PALM STEARIN TENDER - The Egypt's state Food Industries Company said it sought 10,000 tonnes of Malaysian or Indonesian palm stearin for March delivery. The tender will close at 1000 GMT on February 12.
MARKET TALK - China has sold at least 300,000 tonnes of corn recently, marking its return to the world market as an exporter, the head of USDA's Foreign Agriculture Service said.
- French oilseeds and protein seed association SIDO raised its estimate for 1996/97 soybean imports to 750,000 tonnes from a November target of 680,000.
- Italy's autumn durum wheat sowings in the 1996/97 crop season were seen rising 1.5 percent to some 1.70 million hectares, the Italian institute for agriculture studies said.

- China, re-emerging as a corn exporter, apparently sold 250,000 tonnes to the Philippines, South Korea and Malaysia, USDA officials said. Prices were competitive with the U.S., and Asia is seen as the likely market
